hero.title: Operations and Supply Chain: make work flow
hero.subtitle: Find bottlenecks, calculate order quantities, forecast demand and compare suppliers in a working spreadsheet, and write improvement proposals in a document editor. Every task is checked and explained.

activities.title: Map and improve a process
activities.objective: Describe a process step by step, find the bottleneck and propose an improvement.
activities.scenario: A small tailoring shop takes 5 days to deliver a stitched shirt. Write the current process, the bottleneck and your improvement.
steps: Add Heading 2 sections: Current process, Bottleneck, Improvement.
Under Current process write a numbered list of at least five steps, with times in hours or days.
Under Bottleneck say which step is the slowest and why.
Under Improvement describe one change and estimate the new time saved with a number.
Keep it between 110 and 270 words.

activities.title: Cycle time and capacity
activities.objective: Find the bottleneck step and the maximum output of a process.
activities.scenario: A small bakery has four steps in sequence, each with a time per cake in minutes and a number of workers. Find each step's capacity per hour and the system's capacity.
steps: In D2 work out the capacity per hour of each step: 60 divided by the minutes per cake, times the number of workers. Fill down to D5.
In B7 find the lowest capacity with MIN: this is the bottleneck's capacity.
In B8 name the bottleneck step with IF (check rows 2 to 5).
In B9 work out the cakes per 8-hour day: the capacity times 8.

checks.label: D2 is the capacity of the first step
checks.explain: 60 minutes divided by the time per cake, times workers.

checks.label: D3 is the oven capacity
checks.hint: Fill down.

checks.label: D4 is the decorating capacity
checks.hint: Fill down.

checks.label: B7 is the system capacity
checks.hint: =MIN(D2:D5)
checks.explain: A chain moves at the speed of its slowest link.

checks.label: B8 names the bottleneck
checks.explain: Match the minimum to its step.

checks.label: B9 is the day's output
checks.hint: Multiply the system capacity by 8 hours.

activities.title: Economic order quantity
activities.objective: Calculate how much to order at a time to balance ordering and holding costs.
activities.scenario: A shop sells 2,400 units a year. Each order costs 300 rupees to place, and holding one unit for a year costs 12 rupees. Work out the economic order quantity (EOQ) and the yearly cost.
steps: In B6 work out EOQ: the square root of (2 times demand times order cost divided by holding cost) using SQRT.
In B7 work out the number of orders a year: demand divided by EOQ.
In B8 work out the yearly ordering cost: orders times the order cost.
In B9 work out the yearly holding cost: EOQ divided by 2 times holding cost.
In B10 total the two.
In B11 work out the yearly cost if the shop orders 1,200 units at a time instead and show whether EOQ is cheaper in B12.

checks.label: B6 is the EOQ
checks.hint: =SQRT(2*B1*B2/B3)

checks.label: B8 is the ordering cost
checks.explain: Orders times the cost per order.

checks.label: B9 is the holding cost
checks.explain: Average stock is half the order size.

checks.label: B11 is the cost of ordering 1,200 at a time
checks.explain: Same formula with a different order size.

checks.label: B12 compares
checks.explain: EOQ should be the cheaper choice.

cells.A3: Holding cost per unit per year
cells.A11: Cost if ordering 1,200 at a time

activities.title: Forecast demand and set safety stock
activities.objective: Use a moving average to forecast demand and a simple safety-stock rule.
activities.scenario: A shop has six weeks of sales. Forecast the next week using a 3-week moving average, and set a reorder point.
steps: In C5 work out the 3-week moving average of weeks 2 to 4: AVERAGE of B2 to B4. Fill down to C7.
In B9 forecast week 7 as the average of the last three weeks (B5:B7).
In B10 find the standard deviation of weekly sales with STDEV.
In B11 set safety stock as 1.65 times STDEV (about 95% service) rounded up with ROUNDUP.
In B12 set the reorder point: lead-time demand (forecast times lead time in weeks in B8) plus safety stock.

checks.label: C5 is the average of weeks 1 to 3
checks.hint: =AVERAGE(B2:B4)

checks.label: C7 is filled
checks.hint: Fill down.
checks.explain: A moving average slides along the data.

checks.label: B9 forecasts week 7
checks.hint: =AVERAGE(B5:B7)
checks.explain: Average of the last three weeks.

checks.label: B10 is the standard deviation
checks.hint: =STDEV(B2:B7)
checks.explain: A measure of how much sales vary.

checks.label: B11 is the safety stock
checks.hint: =ROUNDUP(1.65*B10,0)
checks.explain: 1.65 standard deviations covers about 95% of cases.

activities.title: Defect rates and a control limit
activities.objective: Calculate defect rates, the average and simple control limits to spot unusual days.
activities.scenario: A factory checks 500 items a day. Work out the defect rate each day, the average, and control limits at the average plus or minus 3 standard deviations.
steps: In C2 work out the defect rate: defects divided by checked. Fill down to C8.
In B10 find the average rate with AVERAGE.
In B11 find the standard deviation of the rates with STDEV.
In B12 set the upper limit: average plus 3 times the standard deviation.
In B13 set the lower limit (not below zero): the larger of 0 and average minus 3 times the standard deviation, using IF.
In D2 show Check if the day's rate is above the upper limit, otherwise OK; fill down.

checks.label: C6 is Friday's rate
checks.hint: Fill down.

checks.label: B10 is the average rate
checks.hint: =AVERAGE(C2:C8)
checks.explain: The mean of the seven rates.

checks.label: B11 is the standard deviation
checks.hint: =STDEV(C2:C8)

checks.label: B13 is the lower limit
checks.explain: A rate cannot be below zero.

activities.title: Compare suppliers by total cost
activities.objective: Compare suppliers using total landed cost, not just the quoted price.
activities.scenario: Two suppliers quote for 1,000 units. One is cheaper but far away. Compare the total cost including transport, duty, delay costs and defects.
steps: In B8 work out the total cost of Supplier A: price times units plus transport plus duty plus the cost of defects (defect rate times units times unit price).
Do the same for Supplier B in C8.
In B9 and C9 work out the cost per usable unit: total cost divided by usable units (units times 1 minus defect rate).
In B10 name the cheaper supplier per usable unit with IF.

checks.label: B8 is Supplier A's total cost
checks.explain: Price, transport, duty, defects and risk.

checks.label: C8 is Supplier B's total cost
checks.hint: Same formula in column C.

checks.label: B9 is A's cost per usable unit
C9 is B's cost per usable unit
B10 names the cheaper supplier
checks.hint: =IF(B9<C9,"Supplier A","Supplier B")
checks.explain: The lower cost per usable unit wins on cost.

activities.title: Write an improvement proposal
activities.objective: Propose an operations improvement with a problem, evidence, solution, cost, benefit and risk.
activities.scenario: A small factory wastes 8% of its raw material. Propose an improvement.
steps: Add a Heading 1 'Improvement proposal'.
Add Heading 2 sections: Problem and evidence, Proposed change, Cost and benefit, Risks, Next steps.
Include at least two numbers in Problem and evidence.
In Cost and benefit give the cost in rupees and the expected yearly saving.
List two or more next steps in a numbered list.
Keep it between 140 and 320 words.

activities.title: Final project: an operations review
activities.objective: Review a small operation, identify the main problem and recommend changes with numbers.
activities.scenario: A bakery delivers 40 orders a day, but 25% arrive late, 6% of cakes are returned and ingredients often run out. Write an operations review.
steps: Add a Heading 1 'Operations review: Sweet Corner Bakery'.
Add Heading 2 sections: Summary, Findings, Recommendations, Expected results, Measures.
In Findings list at least three findings with numbers.
In Recommendations write a numbered list of at least three actions.
In Measures list at least three indicators with targets.
Keep it between 170 and 380 words.
